newsitem.title: GERMANY: German car output growth seen slowing in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German car output growth seen slowing in 1997.

text.p: The German car industry will grow about only half as fast in 1997 as it did this year, the market research firm Marketing Systems said.
Marketing Systems said that new car registrations were likely to expand by around three percent after an unexpectedly strong six percent rate of growth in 1996.
German car production is likely to climb around two percent to 4.62 million units next year, down from four percent growth in 1996, the report said.
Marketing Systems said upcoming new models of the Volkswagen AG Golf and Opel Astra, two of the nation's best-selling cars, will hurt demand next year.
Demand often weakens just before a new model is released because consumers hold off purchases in order to have the most recent car available .
The institute explained that demand in 1996 was stronger than expected. Consumers, it said, had pent up demand for cars after delaying purchases during a recently weak economy.
